prompt: What does `prompts/review.txt` ask the model to judge?
hint: Read its last line.

choices.text: The format and the category
choices.why: Right: urgency is not asked about, so it does not count here.

choices.text: The category and the urgency
choices.why: Urgency is not in the question.

choices.text: Whether the summary is a fair account of what the customer asked for
choices.why: The summary is not judged.

choices.text: Everything the triage prompt asked for
choices.why: It asks about two things, not all of them.

prompt: In which of these cases does the stand-in's review say WRONG? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three cases, all about what it can see.

choices.text: The answer does not parse
choices.why: Yes: the first thing it checks.

choices.text: Its own top label differs from the answer's
choices.why: Yes: it would have said something else.

choices.text: Its two best labels are close
choices.why: Yes: it doubts a close call.

choices.text: The answer disagrees with the person's label
choices.why: It never sees the person's label; that is what makes the check worth measuring.

prompt: Why does the lesson call a self-check *the same opinion asked for twice*?
hint: What does the reviewer know that the first call did not?

choices.text: The reviewer is shown the person's label
choices.why: Nobody shows it the label; it only sees the message and the answer.

choices.text: It reads with what it knew the first time, and nothing new
choices.why: Right: what it adds depends on what differs between the two readings.

choices.text: It runs at a higher temperature
choices.why: The review is not sampled.

choices.text: Because `pl selfcheck` calls the model twice per reply
choices.why: It makes one review call per reply; the phrase is about what the call knows.

prompt: On the temperature-0 run, the check flagged 11 replies and 8 of them were really wrong. What is its precision? Two decimal places.
hint: Right flags over all flags.

prompt: Fourteen replies were really wrong and the check flagged 8 of them. What is its recall? Two decimal places.
hint: Flagged mistakes over all mistakes.

prompt: The six label mistakes the reviewer caught were all flagged *it could also be*, and none of its suggested alternatives was the person's label. What is such a flag good for?
hint: Did it know what the label should be?

choices.text: Replacing the answer with the suggestion
choices.why: That would swap six wrong labels for six other wrong ones.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: Eight of its eleven flags were on real mistakes.

choices.text: Saying the answer was shaky, so a person looks
choices.why: Right: a useful flag and a useless correction.

choices.text: Proving that the person who labelled those six cases made a mistake
choices.why: The reviewer's alternatives were the ones that disagreed with everybody.

prompt: `h27`, a stolen gift card balance, was answered billing and the review said OK. Why did the review miss it?
hint: What does the reviewer read in the message?

choices.text: It reads `card` again and agrees with itself
choices.why: Right: a mistake it would make again is one it cannot see.

choices.text: The reply was not valid JSON
choices.why: It parsed; the label was the problem.

choices.text: The review prompt does not include the message, only the answer
choices.why: It includes both, inside tags.

choices.text: Gift cards are not in any category
choices.why: A person put it in account.

prompt: Of the replies a check flags, the share that were really wrong is its ___.
hint: Its partner is recall.

prompt: The three false alarms, `t37`, `h07` and `h30`, were answered correctly. What were they, to the reviewer?
hint: Same mechanism as the six it caught.

choices.text: Replies that did not parse
choices.why: Those were `t26` and `t39`, and they were really wrong.

choices.text: Messages from the holdout set, which the review prompt does not see
choices.why: `t37` is a dev case, and the review sees every message.

choices.text: Close calls, doubted though right
choices.why: Right: a flag means a close call, which is not the same as a wrong answer.

choices.text: Answers it would have labelled differently
choices.why: Then it would have said *should be*, not *could also be*.

prompt: On the run with five samples per message at temperature 0.8, what recall did the same check reach?
hint: The last line of the table.

prompt: The checker was identical, yet recall rose from 0.57 to 0.84 on the sampled run. Why?
hint: What kind of mistake does sampling add?

choices.text: The review is sampled too, so it catches more by chance
choices.why: The review is not sampled; that is why it sees the favoured label.

choices.text: Mostly slips, which the reviewer sees
choices.why: Right: the run's mistakes changed, and slips are what a self-check catches.

choices.text: 350 replies are a larger sample than 70
choices.why: Size changes how precise the estimate is, not what it estimates.

choices.text: At temperature 0.8 the replies are not JSON
choices.why: Almost all of them parse.

prompt: On `h27` in the sampled run, one sample answered account, the person's label. What did the reviewer say about it?
hint: It reviews by its own belief.

choices.text: OK
choices.why: It passed the four billing samples, not this one.

choices.text: *It could also be billing*
choices.why: It was surer than that.

choices.text: That the answer was not valid JSON
choices.why: It parsed.

choices.text: *The category should be billing*
choices.why: Right: it argued a right answer back to the wrong one.

prompt: What did *Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet* (Huang and others, 2023) find?
hint: Self-correction with no outside information.

choices.text: Self-correction reliably fixed reasoning mistakes
choices.why: The title says the opposite.

choices.text: Little or no gain, and at times a right answer made wrong
choices.why: Right, and it noted that some earlier successes had relied on knowing from outside when an answer was wrong.

choices.text: Self-correction only works at temperature 0
choices.why: That is not what it measured.

choices.text: Models refuse to review their own answers
choices.why: They review them; the question is whether it helps.

prompt: You will ship at temperature 0. A colleague measured a self-check at recall 0.84 on sampled outputs. What do you conclude?
hint: Recall depends on which mistakes the run makes.

choices.text: Expect about 0.84 in production
choices.why: In this lab the same check got 0.57 at temperature 0.

choices.text: Raise the temperature in production so the check catches more
choices.why: That adds mistakes to catch; the answers get worse.

choices.text: Measure it again at temperature 0
choices.why: Right: measure the check on the configuration you ship.

choices.text: Recall is meaningless for a self-check
choices.why: It is meaningful; it is just specific to the run.

prompt: The self-check flagged `t26` and `t39` because they were not JSON. What else finds them?
hint: No model needed.

choices.text: A person reading every reply
choices.why: Possible, and far more expensive than a line of code.

choices.text: The `json` check, exactly and for free
choices.why: Right: `json.loads` fails, with no call and no doubt.

choices.text: A second self-check
choices.why: Another call to do what parsing does.

choices.text: Nothing else; only a model notices format
choices.why: Format is the easiest thing a program checks.

prompt: Which of these can code check exactly, without a model? Choose all that apply.
hint: Anything with a right answer a program can compute.

choices.text: The reply parses as JSON
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The category is one of the five labels
choices.why: Yes: membership in a list.

choices.text: The reply does not contain the canary word
choices.why: Yes: `pl check --canary`.

choices.text: The category is the right reading of the message
choices.why: That is the one question a model check is for.

prompt: Your self-check has precision 0.73 and recall 0.57. What should a flag do in the pipeline?
hint: What did its suggestions turn out to be?

choices.text: Replace the answer with the reviewer's suggestion
choices.why: Here that swaps six wrong labels for six other wrong ones.

choices.text: Send the reply to a person
choices.why: Right: eleven messages read, eight worth reading.

choices.text: Drop the reply silently and move on to the next message in the queue
choices.why: Three of the flagged replies were right, and the customer still needs an answer.

choices.text: Ask the same reviewer again
choices.why: It will say the same thing.

prompt: Which reviewer is most likely to catch the mistakes the answering model makes again and again?
hint: Lesson 19: what makes voters useful?

choices.text: The same model, asked more politely
choices.why: Its view of the message has not changed.

choices.text: The same model at temperature 0.8
choices.why: Sampling the reviewer adds noise, not knowledge.

choices.text: The same model with the review prompt repeated three times
choices.why: Three identical readings are one reading.

choices.text: A different model, or one given new evidence
choices.why: Right: a reviewer with different blind spots misses different things.

prompt: Put the stages of checking a reply in the order this lesson recommends.
hint: Cheapest and exact first.
items: Code checks parsing, fields, labels and the canary
The model checks whether the label fits the message
A person reads what was flagged

prompt: Match each term to what it means in this lesson.
hint: Four terms.

pairs.right: Share of flags that were really wrong
Share of mistakes that were flagged
A sample that missed the label the model favours
The model favours the wrong label

prompt: A team adds a self-check to a temperature-0 pipeline and reports that it *finds most mistakes*, from a demo of five sampled answers. What do you ask for first?
hint: What would this lesson's table look like on their configuration?

choices.text: Precision and recall against a person's labels, at temperature 0
choices.why: Right: measured on what ships, against labels nobody's model wrote.

choices.text: A longer review prompt
choices.why: Length is not evidence.

choices.text: Five more sampled answers
choices.why: More samples measure the wrong configuration better.

choices.text: The reviewer's own confidence in its verdicts
choices.why: Lesson 21 shows how far a stated confidence can be trusted.
